issue_context.title: Automatically handle `HEAD` requests in `GET` handler unless explicit `HEAD` handler exists
issue_context.body:
<!--
Before you submit an issue we recommend you visit [Fastify Help](https://github.com/fastify/help) and ask any questions you have or mention any problems you've had getting started with Fastify.

**Please read this entire template before posting any issue. If you ignore these instructions
and post an issue here that does not follow the instructions, your issue might be closed,
locked, and assigned the `missing discussion` label.**
-->

## 🚀 Feature Proposal

Fastify does not automatically handle `HEAD` requests in `GET` handlers, unlike Express.

From [`express`' docs](https://expressjs.com/en/api.html#app.METHOD)

>The `app.get()` function is automatically called for the HTTP `HEAD` method in addition to the `GET` method if `app.head()` was not called for the path before `app.get()`.

I think it makes sense for Fastify to do the same (possibly via some option?).

From [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypertext_Transfer_Protocol#Request_methods)

>The HEAD method asks for a response identical to that of a GET request, but without the response body. This is useful for retrieving meta-information written in response headers, without having to transport the entire content.

As mentioned in https://github.com/fastify/fastify/issues/2061#issuecomment-579848040, `express` just skips sending the body on `HEAD` (via `send`).

I tried to find some issue where this was discussed without finding one. Apologies if this has already been discussed.

## Motivation

Forcing the user to use two handlers (or pass `methods: ['GET', 'HEAD'])` to `fastify.route`) when we almost always have to do the same thing in the handlers (e.g. we need `content-length` header, so the only real difference in the handlers is often if body is sent or not - the user would still have to _construct_ the body) seems unnecessary to me. We also have to manually set the `content-length` header now for the body.

## Example

```js
const express = require('express')();
const fastify = require('fastify')();

express.get('/hello', (_, res) => {
  res.send('hi from express');
});

fastify.get('/hello', (_, reply) => {
  reply.send('hi from fastify');
});

express.listen(3000);
fastify.listen(3001);
```

```sh-session
$ curl -i http://localhost:3000/hello
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-Powered-By: Express
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 15
ETag: W/"f-JpU+vo3voFR+FPycQwU/gyiCSag"
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2020 12:20:54 GMT
Connection: keep-alive
Keep-Alive: timeout=5

hi from express%                                                                                                                                                                                                                               

$ curl -i http://localhost:3001/hello
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: text/plain; charset=utf-8
content-length: 15
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2020 12:20:56 GMT
Connection: keep-alive
Keep-Alive: timeout=5

hi from fastify%                                                                                                                                                                                                                               

$ curl -I http://localhost:3000/hello
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-Powered-By: Express
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 15
ETag: W/"f-JpU+vo3voFR+FPycQwU/gyiCSag"
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2020 12:20:59 GMT
Connection: keep-alive
Keep-Alive: timeout=5

$ curl -I http://localhost:3001/hello
HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
content-type: application/json; charset=utf-8
content-length: 78
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2020 12:21:02 GMT
Connection: keep-alive
Keep-Alive: timeout=5
```

If this change were to be implemented that last request would be correct out of the box.
comments: I'm +1 on this. However, this feature should have a great doc and able to unsubscribe the HEAD requests for some reason.

> possibly via some option?

Would a plugin be a solution?

A plugin could decorate the `fastify` instance with a new method:

```
fastify.getPlusHead('/url', handler) // not so nice this method name
```

that does the boring work:

- register the routes
- manage the content-length header
I like the idea, but I think it should definitely live in a plugin that does this behind the scenes, very likely by using the `onRoute` hook.

I agree with @delvedor, this can be implemented in a plugin that defines a new route for every get defined. It can alter the body via a custom `onSend` header or by calling the other route via `inject()`.
Is there any process to create a plugin repo? I would like to contribute more often and this sounds like a good weekend project if it's not already done
Take a look at one of the examples in this org... https://github.com/fastify/fastify-cookie is a great example.

Thanks! I used it as a starting point!
I've played for a while on it and I'm a little bit stuck. I'm seeing from [here](https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/e29411bd7e2f448ad7edd8ceec18e593816a02e6/lib/reply.js#L389) that "organically" (returning or calling `reply.send` In the handler or calling `done()` from the `onSend` hook) there's no way to manually set the `content-length` header by either the handler or the `onSend` hook. In case we want to preserve the `content-length`, there's a workaround to achieve it or I'm missing something I don't know?
You found a bug in Fastify! Good spot. Would you like to send a PR to add `req.method === 'HEAD'` as part of that conditional?
Oh wow, amazing! Sure, I'll open a PR with the proper tests then 😄
Waiting for #2651 to be able to continue with the plugin
@MetCoder95 please keep this issue updated with your progress with the plugin 🙂
Sure! I'll continue it during the weekend 🙂

I almost finish the plugin, it's just about finishing adding tests and the documentation 😄 
Just a couple of questions:

- Should I make a repo in my profile and upload it or how should I handle this part?
- How should we handle streams, it's not possible to know the full length without waiting for it to finish, or do I'm missing something?

Go ahead and create a fresh repo! Use fastify-cookie as a guideline if you need one.

Streams without a Content-Length implies a chunked transfer encoding. They should definitely be handled... I think we'd need to call .resume() on the stream and count how many bytes flow through.
Then ok, we don't need to count. We should still call `.resume()` on the stream.
Yep and remove `Transfer-Encoding`?
I think that is set by Node.js internals, so we should not worry about it.

Got it, thanks a lot for the input I'll move it in that way then 👍 

There's not `transfer-encoding` at all at the response when removing the body from the response body. e.g.
```javascript
  headers: {
    'content-type': 'application/octet-stream',
    date: 'Mon, 02 Nov 2020 22:41:17 GMT',
    connection: 'keep-alive'
  }
```

So, I think we're good then. I'm going to also remove the `content-type` to follow the Express response

I already opened a small [PR](https://github.com/MetCoder95/fastify-get-head/pull/1) with the first implementation. I didn't implement any CI or issue template but will do it in different PRs. Of course, all feedback is welcome (also name change, I'm not totally sure about the name 😅 ). Thanks!

Hi! Thanks again for the full support during the process! I think the plugin it's done, feel free to take a look here: https://github.com/MetCoder95/fastify-get-head

Also, feel free if at some point you want to take it into fastify org 👍 

Is there anything remaining? 😄
Would you mind to send a PR to update the ecosystem page?
Sure, I'll do it 👍
The PR is merged :)

WRT this not being default behavior - I still think that's a mistake.

- Express does it by default: https://expressjs.com/en/api.html#app.METHOD
- Koa does it by default: couldn't find docs, but run https://www.digitalocean.com/community/tutorials/how-to-build-a-hello-world-application-with-koa
- Spring does it by default: https://docs.spring.io/spring-framework/docs/current/reference/html/web.html#mvc-ann-requestmapping-head-options
- Python does it by default: https://docs.python.org/3/library/http.server.html
- Go does it by default: couldn't find docs, run this example https://yourbasic.org/golang/http-server-example/

Node core (technically it does since it's a single handler that doesn't care about request method) and Ruby (I'm assuming Rails does it) are the only ones I found that doesn't.

At the very least I think it should be called out as a gotcha in the docs somewhere that Fastify does not do this.
I'm happy to revise this decision in v4 - it's definitely a semver-major change.
That makes sense - thanks @mcollina!
Would you like to send a PR that implements it for v4 (target the `next` branch).

In that case, should I move the implementation to `fastify` then? 
Also, I'll change the plugin to only support fastify `>= 3.8 && < 4` just to let others still use the plugin. Sounds good?
yes!

Make the [fix](https://github.com/MetCoder95/fastify-get-head/pull/3) for the plugin, please have a look 😄 
I'll start with the implementation in `next` over the week

Thanks @MetCoder95!

I opened up a separate #2692 for the `onSend` bug

No worries 🙏 

I opened a PR #2700 to close the issue. Sadly it has collateral damage on other tests, I'll adjust them even that there's a couple that I'm quite missed about why are they failing. Please have a look and let me know your feedback 🙂

review_comments:
Did you evaluate to use `preSerialization`?

If the GET has a HUGE payload, it will be serialized with this implementation and then discarded.
Maybe could it be possible to avoid this process step?

Hmm, actually didn't think about it but sounds logical to me. The only thing is that will not handle payloads where `streams`, `buffers` or `strings` are being sent (even `null`), for those cases `onSend` hook will still be needed, isn't it?
Maybe appending handlers for both hooks will cover both scenarios, what do you think?
I don't think it's possible to avoid it. HEAD request should return the `content-length` header, and it's impossible to compute it _without_ serializing.
use strict is missing on top
Just a thought: if there is a HEAD route and the user sets the route level option `hasRouteExposeHeadRouteFlag` too, would it be too harsh logging a warning?
Don't think so, would be just adding an `else if` to see if the `headRouteExists` and `hasRouteExposedHeadRouteFlag` it's set to `true` for printing the warning. What do you think?

I think it could let users say "oh gosh, it saves me a bad headache"
If you have the chance to add it, I think it will be really appreciated by someone!
haha, sure! No issue at all, I think will save someone's day, let me add it 😄

Done in 976b080
Please have a look 🙂
You'll need to add an `on('error')` handler. Also add a test for this case.
Curious, should throw in case of an error or just use the logger to show it up?
You need to call the callback `done(err)`.

Now that I look at it is a bit more complex. Sorry about the wrong turn - you should not call the callback because it would make it call the callback twice which is not really something we want.

You should just log the error - the response was already sent, so there is nothing else to do.
No worries, I think that also explains why was quite hard to test. Turning it into a log output then
